room.name: Hearthwatch Keep Courtyard
room.description: The military keep stands at the heart of Hearthwatch Crossing: a ringed stone courtyard of banner poles, drill lines, petition benches, messenger ravens, and a bronze bell that rang by itself when the dead star appeared. Six crowded districts press against the keep walls, each with its own laws, smells, accents, grudges, and rumors.

object.name: Dead-Star Bell
object.description: A cracked bronze bell hangs above the keep gate. No rope touches it, yet townsfolk swear it rang at noon under a black star.
object.interact_text: You compare soot marks, old consecration sigils, and fresh frost along the bell mouth, confirming the omen touched the keep before the rest of town.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Keep Council Hall
room.description: A narrow hall of war maps, civic ledgers, oath tablets, and oil portraits. Matron Velia holds open court here while soldiers, merchants, priests, and petitioners argue over which crisis deserves the next lantern patrol.

object.name: War Table of the Marches
object.description: Painted roads and brass pins mark every zone that can eventually lead toward the Astral Crown Citadel.
object.interact_text: You study the pins and note which factions control each road, unlocking better context for the long campaign.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Keep Muster Yard
room.description: Soldiers spar beside supply wagons while healers check bandages and quartermasters count arrows. The yard makes the town feel defended, but not safe; too many squads are already missing on the old roads.

object.name: Lantern Post Rack
object.description: Fresh road lanterns wait beside old ones etched with warding scripture.
object.interact_text: You test the oil, glass, and silver wick housings, learning why the northern posts failed before the first adventure route.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Hearthwatch Keep Lockup
room.description: The lockup sits below the keep rather than under the market now: clean cells, chalked charges, a shrine to fair judgment, and one barred interview room used for spies, smugglers, and magically confused goats.

object.name: Prisoner Tally Slate
object.description: Names and offenses are written with unusual care. Several arrests involve the same phrase: “heard the star whisper.”
object.interact_text: You copy the repeated phrase and mark it as evidence for the dead-star investigation.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Residential District: Hearth Commons
room.description: Laundry lines, chicken coops, public ovens, shared wells, children with wooden swords, tired parents, retired caravan guards, and rented rooms crowd the southern district. The Bronze Bell Inn anchors the common life of the town.

object.name: Commons Story Well
object.description: Every household draws water here, so every rumor eventually returns to the bucket rope.
object.interact_text: You listen long enough to separate frightened invention from useful witness statements.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Residential District: Bellfounder Lane
room.description: Narrow workshops make hinge pins, buckles, cooking hooks, shrine bells, and cheap armor rivets. Dwarven apprentices, human widows, goblin cousins, and goliath teamsters all shout over the furnace bellows.

object.name: Cracked Handbell Mold
object.description: A bell mold split down the center at the same moment the keep bell rang.
object.interact_text: You compare the fracture to the keep bell and confirm both cracks point toward the arcane district observatory.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Bronze Bell Inn
room.description: The inn is packed with caravan guards, minstrels, muleteers, pilgrims, retired adventurers, and one table that always seems to know more than it says. Its common room now serves as the social switchboard for every district.

object.name: Rumor Table
object.description: A scarred round table where guards, dockhands, nobles in plain cloaks, and apprentices trade claims about the dead star.
object.interact_text: You take time to investigate, gathering rumors from all six districts and a small advantage for the road ahead.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Bronze Bell Guest Rooms
room.description: A row of rented rooms offers patched quilts, secure trunks, private lockboxes, and enough quiet to count arrows or study spell formulae while the town murmurs below.

room.name: Noble District: Aurelian Terrace
room.description: Terraced manors overlook the keep from the north: rose hedges, watchful servants, hired duelists, inheritance banners, and polished doors that open more easily for titles than truth.

object.name: Sealed Invitation Wall
object.description: Wax-sealed notices announce donations, alliances, and carefully phrased accusations among the noble houses.
object.interact_text: You read the public notices and spot which noble families are quietly preparing to leave town.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Noble District: Auric House Parlor
room.description: A parlor of gold-thread carpets, crystal lamps, ancestral weapons, and servants who hear everything while appearing to hear nothing. The nobility fear the dead star, but fear public panic even more.

object.name: Ancestor Blade Case
object.description: A display case holds blades carried during the first sealing of the Astral Crown.
object.interact_text: You notice one blade has been recently removed, suggesting a noble house knows more about the old war than it admits.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Noble District: Council Garden
room.description: A formal garden between the terrace and council hall gives merchants, priests, nobles, and militia captains a polite place to threaten each other under trimmed yew arches.

object.name: Stone Oath Bench
object.description: Local treaties are carved into the bench arms in Common, Elvish, Dwarvish, and Halfling.
object.interact_text: You trace the oldest treaty and learn that Hearthwatch was founded as a military sanctuary, not just a trade stop.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Market District: Lantern Arcade
room.description: Canvas stalls crowd a covered lane where dwarven smiths, elven vintners, human bakers, goblin tinkers, dragonborn porters, and tiefling map-sellers haggle under colored lamps. The market keeps the hub economically alive.

object.name: Market Well
object.description: A crowded well where gossip, bribes, job notices, and arguments over bread prices all pass through the same hands.
object.interact_text: You gather enough accounts to understand which districts are frightened, profiting, or hiding something.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Market District: Guildhall of Measures
room.description: The guildhall smells of beeswax, ink, flour dust, and coin. Its counters certify weights, caravan shares, construction bids, and mercenary contracts under the watch of neutral clerks.

object.name: Contract Ledger
object.description: Open contracts show missing wagons, delayed grain, and several suspicious payments routed through shell caravans.
object.interact_text: You mark three contracts that tie the warehouse district to noble money and road disappearances.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Market District: Adventurers Exchange
room.description: A job board, gear cages, sparring mat, trophy wall, and curse-disclaimer desk serve sellswords, pilgrims, and young heroes who do not yet know which warnings are serious.

object.name: Expanded Notice Board
object.description: The old notice board has grown into a formal exchange with district jobs, escort requests, monster bounties, and missing-person notes.
object.interact_text: You sort beginner work from bait, finding hooks for the road lanterns, warehouse manifest, and six-district orientation.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Warehouse District: River Gate
room.description: A stone bridge and customs gate watch the silver river, where barges unload salt, wool, timber, refugees, smuggled relics, and rumors from distant trouble. The warehouse district controls what enters Hearthwatch.

object.name: Customs Manifest
object.description: A daybook lists cargo by captain, crate mark, and tax seal. Several entries have been scraped clean and rewritten.
object.interact_text: You recover enough overwritten ink to identify a hidden shipment connected to the dead-star omen.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Warehouse District: Lantern Quay
room.description: Cranes creak above wet planks, bonded warehouses, fishmongers, river priests, stevedores, smugglers, and Marchwarden patrols pretending not to watch the same locked doors.

object.name: Marked Crate Stack
object.description: Several crates bear a crown-shaped burn mark hidden beneath shipping chalk.
object.interact_text: You pry away the chalk and confirm the Crownless Cabal has agents moving goods through Hearthwatch.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Warehouse District: Customs Vault
room.description: Below the river gate, confiscated relics, cursed antiques, unpaid cargo, and judicial evidence sit behind iron grates and warded ledgers. The vault touches the lockup by a guarded service stair.

object.name: Confiscated Relic Case
object.description: A sealed case pulses faintly when the dead star is visible through the river grates.
object.interact_text: You identify the pulse as sympathetic resonance with the Astral Crown relic-chain.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Warehouse District: Ferry Landing
room.description: Flat-bottom river boats knock against mossy pylons while a shuttered coastal ticket window gathers dust. The local boats still run north toward Greenbarrow, but the long Tidebound ferry to Terrecester Wharf requires a ticket sold only at the far-shore office.

object.name: River Mist Marker
object.description: Old ferry marks distinguish natural fog from spirit mist. Today, one mark has turned black.
object.interact_text: You learn which mist signs point toward Greenbarrow and which point back toward Hearthwatch’s arcane problem.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

object.name: Closed Coast Ticket Window
object.description: The blue-painted Tidebound ticket booth is shuttered from the outside. A chalk sign reads: “Terrecester office active. Hearthwatch sales suspended by league order.”
object.interact_text: You confirm there is no way to buy a Tidebound coastal ticket here. The route can only be opened after reaching Terrecester Wharf by the proper road.
object.completed_text: The closed office remains closed; only a Terrecester-issued ticket will satisfy the ferrymen.

room.name: Temple District: Row of Six Lamps
room.description: Small shrines share a long colonnade; incense, public arguments, charity lines, funeral bells, and quiet acts of mercy pass from one altar to the next. The district welcomes every lawful faith that keeps a lamp for travelers.

object.name: Oath Brazier
object.description: An ever-lit brazier where Marchwardens, merchants, and pilgrims swear public promises before taking the roads.
object.interact_text: You read the ash patterns and find signs that someone recently swore a false oath under magical pressure.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Temple District: Mercy Cloister
room.description: A sheltered court of bedrolls, soup kettles, herb gardens, and recovery cots. Refugees from the roads bring warnings long before officials admit those warnings are data.

object.name: Patient Witness Cots
object.description: Wounded travelers mutter about black lanterns, singing stones, and skeletal riders outside mapped roads.
object.interact_text: You gently interview the patients and add their route fragments to the war table evidence.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Temple District: Oath Brazier Sanctum
room.description: Behind bronze doors, a sanctum holds vow tablets, reliquary lamps, and an old ward-stone that hums when undead cross any road sworn to the Marchwardens.

object.name: Ancient Ward-Stone
object.description: The ward-stone is older than Hearthwatch and bears a sunburst crown deliberately chiseled away.
object.interact_text: You confirm the town was built over one of the minor anchors of the ancient Astral Crown seal.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Arcane District: Concordium Lanternhouse
room.description: Silver Concord mages maintain blue-flame street lanterns, divination mirrors, message ravens, and polite warning signs about unstable portals. The arcane district sits between scholarship and civic paranoia.

object.name: Blue-Flame Lantern Array
object.description: A grid of lanterns burns blue where ordinary flames should be gold. Some flicker in the pattern of a constellation no one charted.
object.interact_text: You calibrate the array and reveal a star-path pointing toward the first outer relics.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Arcane District: Spellwright Lane
room.description: Scroll sellers, wand-lacquerers, component grinders, familiar groomers, and mage apprentices crowd a lane where every third sign insists the last explosion was planned.

object.name: Unstable Scroll Press
object.description: A spell press judders under too much astral static.
object.interact_text: You vent the static safely, earning the spellwrights’ gratitude and a cleaner reading of the dead-star resonance.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Arcane District: Subterranean Glyph Archive
room.description: A cool underground archive stores rubbings of stones, dead languages, forbidden seals, and field reports from every dangerous place the Silver Concord pretends it merely studies.

object.name: Names of the Dead Shelf
object.description: A shelf of war-dead registers includes names scratched out by the same hand across three centuries.
object.interact_text: You restore several names with dusting powder, giving Scribe Miravel evidence of Cabal memory-magic.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Arcane District: Starfall Observatory
room.description: An open-roof observatory crowns the lanternhouse. Brass lenses, celestial wheels, and bound air elementals track a dead star that casts no light but still throws a shadow across every warded map.

object.name: Dead-Star Astrolabe
object.description: The astrolabe refuses ordinary constellations and points instead to places where old relics sleep.
object.interact_text: You align the instrument and confirm Hearthwatch is the campaign’s first anchor in a much larger ward network.
object.completed_text: This feature has already yielded its secret.

room.name: Greenbarrow Road: Applebough Mile
room.description: The road north of Hearthwatch narrows into wagon-rutted apple country. Low stone walls divide pea fields and barley strips; painted halfling waystones warn tallfolk to close gates, praise the cook, and never ignore a crow sitting alone on a fencepost.

object.name: Applebough Waystones
object.description: Three waist-high stones are painted with apples, handprints, and the Freehold maxim: Share first, count later.
object.interact_text: You read the road customs and learn why Greenbarrow hospitality is treated as law, not sentiment.
object.completed_text: The waystones have already taught their lesson.

room.name: Roadside Lantern Furrow
room.description: A line of road lanterns leans over bean rows. Several have been stuffed with damp straw and black feathers, a crude attempt to make travelers think the Barrow Freeholds abandoned the road.

room.name: Wayside Shrine of the Full Bowl
room.description: A little open-air shrine shelters a stone bowl kept full of apples, heel-ends of bread, and copper coins. Local children watch from behind the hedge to see whether strangers take one gift or all of them.

room.name: Applewallow South Stile
room.description: A crooked wooden stile marks the village boundary. Fresh ribbons show which kin-houses need help, which barns have room for guests, and which fields are under watch for burrow signs.

room.name: Applewallow Village Green
room.description: Applewallow is a busy halfling farming village built around a sloping green, communal ovens, cider barrels, burrow-door stoops, sheep bells, and an enormous notice board. The place feels small only until you notice how many hands keep it alive.

object.name: Freehold Notice Board
object.description: The board lists lost sheep, pie rotations, patrol rosters, borrowable tools, and three separate warnings about holes opening where holes should not be.
object.interact_text: You read enough notices to understand Applewallow’s troubles: missing grain, disturbed barrows, broken lanterns, and something hungry under the fields.
object.completed_text: You have already read the board and sorted its urgent notes from its gossip.

room.name: Applewallow Common Kitchen
room.description: Six ovens heat one long room filled with steam, gossip, flour, and crisis management. Everyone eats here when danger rises; nobody is allowed to be hungry because pride kept them silent.

room.name: Common Root Cellars
room.description: Packed-earth cellars run beneath half the village. The shelves should smell of onions and apples; today they smell faintly of grave loam and wet fur.

room.name: Cider Market and Tinker Stalls
room.description: Cider presses, seed merchants, knife-grinders, gossiping aunties, and visiting wagoners crowd this packed little market. Prices are argued loudly, but emergency supplies are quietly passed to anyone who needs them.

room.name: Honeybell Bee-Yards
room.description: Painted hives sit among clover and bean flowers. The bees are usually docile enough to nap on a child’s sleeve, but something sour under the soil has made them form warning spirals above the grass.

room.name: Harvest Chapel of Yondalla’s Table
room.description: The chapel is less a temple than a bright kitchen with saints painted on the beams. The altar is a long table; the holiest ritual is setting another chair.

room.name: Burrowhome Lanes
room.description: Round doors open into warm hillside homes with flower boxes, boot scrapers, and roof gardens. The residents have left soup on half the steps and spears behind half the curtains.

room.name: Freehold Grain Co-op
room.description: Every sack in the co-op is marked by household, field, season, and need. The Barrow Freeholds survive by shared stores, so the recent thefts are not mere crime; they are a direct attack on the village’s soul.

room.name: Applewallow Moot Hall
room.description: A low-raftered hall holds benches sized for halflings and stools grudgingly sized for everyone else. Disputes are settled over soup, testimony, and a terrifying ledger of who borrowed whose plough in what year.

room.name: Moot Hall Loft
room.description: Bundles of old banners, festival masks, and militia slings are stored among the rafters. A map of old burrows shows tunnels that should have collapsed generations ago.

room.name: Freehold Militia Post
room.description: Short spears, slingstones, borrowed helmets, kettle shields, and very serious sign-up sheets fill the dugout militia post. These are farmers first, but no one mistakes them for helpless.

room.name: Applebough Orchards
room.description: Old apple trees bend over the path like concerned grandparents. The orchards are loud with workers, ladders, sheepdogs, crows, and the nervous jokes of people refusing to show fear.

room.name: Cloverdown Sheepfolds
room.description: Low pasture walls zigzag across clover hills. The sheep crowd near the shepherds instead of grazing, and the guard geese keep staring at the same harmless patch of earth.

room.name: Miller Stream and Waterwheel
room.description: A shallow stream turns a red-painted waterwheel beside a tidy mill. Muddy tracks crawl up from the bank, circle the grain chute, and vanish into a badger hole too large for any honest badger.

room.name: Clover-Barrow Rise
room.description: Grass-covered burial mounds rise between apple trees and chapel stones. The Freeholds tend the graves with flowers, jokes, and food offerings; the dead are family, not scenery.

room.name: Ancestor Crypt of Shared Loaves
room.description: The crypt walls are carved with family trees, recipes, debts forgiven, and harvest jokes. A colder inscription has been scratched across them: WHAT IS GIVEN CAN BE TAKEN BACK.

room.name: Scarecrow Furrows
room.description: Rows of barley and turnips stretch around scarecrows dressed in patched coats. Several scarecrows have been turned to face Applewallow, their straw hands stuffed with stolen seed labels.

room.name: North Furrows and Badger Runs
room.description: The fields north of Applewallow lose their friendly geometry. Fences sag, furrows split open, and every badger run seems to breathe damp grave air from somewhere below.

room.name: Old Willow Crossing
room.description: An ancient willow grips both banks of a ditch where no water runs. Halfling patrol charms hang from the branches beside claw marks large enough to split a wagon wheel.

room.name: Tenant Copse
room.description: The copse remembers the time before the Freeholds, when the old baron taxed seed, wells, ovens, and mourning. Even the birds go quiet here.

room.name: Elder Barrow Marker
room.description: A ring of little standing stones marks where Applewallow’s first freeholders swore never again to let one lord own another family’s hunger.

object.name: Freehold Oath Stones
object.description: Each stone bears a palmprint and a name. The smallest print is no bigger than a child’s.
object.interact_text: The oath clarifies the zone’s heart: land is tended together, food is shared before it is sold, and no one is left alone to be devoured by winter.
object.completed_text: The oath stones have already shared their meaning.

room.name: The Dire Burrows Mouth
room.description: The entrance to The Dire Burrows gapes beneath the old willow roots. It is too round, too smooth, and ringed with gnawed plough handles, cracked crockery, and little offerings meant to convince the earth to close again.

room.name: Dire Burrows: Lantern Ledge
room.description: The first ledge of the burrows is strung with stolen village lanterns. Their light reveals root-tunnels, clawed chalk marks, and an old baronial seal pressed into the loam like a bad memory.

room.name: Dire Burrows: Mushroom Run
room.description: Pale mushrooms grow from buried fence posts and pantry shelves. Their caps pulse whenever someone speaks the word mine, as if the tunnels prefer ownership to stewardship.

room.name: Dire Burrows: Chittering Nest
room.description: The tunnel widens into a nest of wool scraps, apple seeds, and sharpened bone. Something has trained the burrow vermin to drag food below instead of eating it.

room.name: Dire Burrows: Three-Tine Fork
room.description: Three tunnels split around a buried pitchfork whose handle has sprouted black leaves. Halfling chalk marks point toward safe footing; older noble marks point toward hoards.

room.name: Dire Burrows: Stolen Root Cellar
room.description: The burrow cuts into an old storage chamber. Sacks from half of Applewallow have been sorted by household, not to return them, but to teach each family the pain of being singled out.

room.name: Dire Burrows: Bone Pantry
room.description: Bones of badgers, sheep, and unlucky raiders are stacked beside cracked pie plates. The pantry is not messy; it is inventoried.

room.name: Dire Burrows: Grave-Loam Maze
room.description: A cramped maze of low tunnels winds through roots and burial soil. Freehold carvings mark the true path, but the walls keep rearranging themselves into old tax ledgers and locked pantry doors.

maze.progress_message: You follow the Freehold marks: a bowl, a hand, a loaf, a seed. The loam shifts aside for those who remember sharing.
maze.failure_message: The tunnel pinches inward, every wrong turn sounding like a pantry door being locked. You are returned to the first bend.
maze.success_message: The maze exhales warm earth, opening into a hidden seed cache older than Applewallow itself.

room.name: Dire Burrows: First Seed Cache
room.description: Clay jars of ancestral seed rest in a chamber kept warm by a buried hearthstone. The cache proves the Freeholds began with mutual aid, not conquest.

room.name: Dire Burrows: Fallow Shrine
room.description: A shrine made from a broken plough stands before a black root. Half the offerings are wholesome bread and apples; the other half are contracts, chains, and old noble spoons.

room.name: Dire Burrows: Starved Hall
room.description: The hall is a feasting room turned inside out. Empty plates hang on the walls like shields, and every chair faces a locked grain chest where a throne should be.

room.name: The Dire Burrows: Hoard-Throne of the Unsharing Maw
room.description: The lowest chamber of The Dire Burrows is a stolen granary, a grave, and a throne room at once. Fallowmaw waits among hoarded seed and gnawed bones, promising order through hunger and obedience through isolation.

room.name: North Stile Beyond the Barrows
room.description: Beyond the boss chamber, a narrow tunnel rises into clean air at the northern stile. Apple trees give way to tangled briar country, and the next road waits under darker leaves.

room.name: Root-Toll Hollow
room.description: The Greenbarrow lane narrows beneath living blackthorn, where silver bells hang from roots like fruit. Thorn Court watchers ask no toll in coin; they ask names, promises, and proof that travelers know the difference.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Root-Toll Bells
object.description: A curtain of silver acorn bells chimes only when someone speaks a true intention.
object.interact_text: You give the bells a careful answer. The hollow records your intent, and hidden eyes stop treating you as a trespasser.

room.name: Glimmerhazel Path
room.description: A side path wanders through hazel trees whose leaves show memories instead of reflections. Hunters leave chalk spirals here so they can find the same morning twice.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Memory-Hazel Leaves
object.description: Each leaf holds a scene of some oath once sworn beneath this canopy.
object.interact_text: You press a leaf flat and watch a Thorn Court oath collapse into betrayal, revealing why Onfadell fears the Nameless Oracle.

room.name: Moonmote Causeway
room.description: A raised causeway of pale root-stone crosses a carpet of blue moss. Moonmotes drift between carved faces, lighting the way toward the ancient Fey city at the Briar’s heart.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Moonmote Lanterns
object.description: The lanterns burn with moth-sized stars and shift according to court law.
object.interact_text: You align three lanterns to the old path signs. The causeway reveals the names of safe trees and hungry ones.

room.name: Briar Mere
room.description: A mirror-dark pond lies between reed beds and rose-thorns. The water repeats every spoken word once in truth, once in mockery, and once in a voice that might belong to the future.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Truth-Water Pool
object.description: The surface catches names like fish, but refuses to keep false ones.
object.interact_text: You let the pool test a rumor about the Oracle. The water returns only one phrase: she was named once, and punished for it.

room.name: Vowtree Grove
room.description: Gigantic trees braided with ribbons surround a green tribunal stone. Every ribbon marks a vow; every broken ribbon has grown a thorn sharp enough to draw memory instead of blood.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Broken Vow Ribbons
object.description: Several court-ribbons hang snapped, their cut ends whispering accusations against Onfadell.
object.interact_text: You sort accusation from grief. The intact ribbons identify a false witness serving the Nameless Oracle.

room.name: Name-Taken Ford
room.description: A shallow ford crosses a stream that steals labels from careless travelers. Road signs become blank here, and footprints sometimes continue without their owners.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Blank Milestones
object.description: The milestones are smooth, but the air around them is crowded with missing syllables.
object.interact_text: You trace old letters with briar-silver dust. Three stolen names return to the stones, weakening the Oracle’s reach.

room.name: Onfadell Living Gate
room.description: Onfadell begins as a gate grown from two ancient trees that have chosen to remain doors. Their bark is carved with heraldry, jokes, warnings, and threats from a thousand seasons of Thorn Court rule.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Living Gate Faces
object.description: Wooden faces open and close in the bark, demanding etiquette before passage.
object.interact_text: You answer with the proper greeting: thorn before flower, debt before feast. The gate admits you as a guest, not prey.

room.name: Onfadell Outer Ring
room.description: Curved bridges, root balconies, and green-glass arches circle the city in slow spirals. No street is straight; old Fey magic dislikes being approached too directly.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Spiral Street Marks
object.description: The street marks change for guests, oathbreakers, children, and monarchs.
object.interact_text: You study the spirals until they sort themselves into a map of social standing, revealing which doors will answer you.

room.name: Onfadell Briar Market
room.description: The market trades in honeyed bread, bottled moonlight, curses folded into paper birds, thorn-silk, prophecy ink, and practical socks for people with hooves.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Bargain Pole
object.description: Tokens from hundreds of bargains hang on a pole watched by three suspicious ravens.
object.interact_text: You read the tokens and identify a merchant debt the Oracle has been twisting into a curse.

room.name: Glassroot Residences
room.description: Homes grown from living root and translucent green crystal cluster around communal hearths. Eladrin, dryads, sprites, awakened foxes, changelings, and mortal guests share etiquette more fragile than glass.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Hearth of Many Seasons
object.description: The communal hearth burns winter, spring, summer, and autumn in four separate flames.
object.interact_text: You warm your hands at each flame and learn how the city remembers centuries as neighbors rather than dates.

room.name: Verdant Archive
room.description: Books grow as leaves from branch-shelves, and librarians prune arguments before they become wars. The oldest shelves are sealed in sap because the truth inside remains politically inconvenient.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Sap-Sealed Shelf
object.description: A shelf of amber-sapped leaves hums with suppressed testimony about the Nameless Oracle.
object.interact_text: You soften the sap with moonmote warmth. The leaves reveal that the Oracle once served as Onfadell’s truth-speaker before her name was erased.

room.name: Seat of the Thorn Court
room.description: The seat of Thorn Court power is a crescent amphitheater grown around a white-thorn throne. Nobles sit beside beetle-knights, fox advocates, tree spirits, masked duelists, and petitioners too proud to look frightened.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: White-Thorn Throne
object.description: The throne flowers only when a ruler speaks for the forest rather than themselves.
object.interact_text: You observe which nobles avoid the flowering thorn. Their fear points toward the Oracle’s surviving sympathizers.

room.name: The Lost Orrery: Overgrown Portico
room.description: Behind the Verdant Archive, a domed building leans under centuries of ivy. Its bronze doors show the same dead star that first appeared above Hearthwatch, but here the star is drawn as a wound.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Bronze Star-Doors
object.description: The doors are locked by rotating constellations rather than a keyhole.
object.interact_text: You rotate the wounded-star sigil into alignment with the Marches. The doors breathe open and release the smell of dust and rain.

room.name: The Lost Orrery: Axis Hall
room.description: A central axle of black wood and silver gears rises through the chamber. Each turn of the mechanism casts a different night sky across the walls, some real, some forbidden, some apparently waiting to happen.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Axis of Seasons
object.description: The axis binds moon, root, tide, and star into a single rotating calculation.
object.interact_text: You set the season to the night of the dead star. A hidden projection shows the Astral Crown Citadel pulling at the Marches through old ward-lines.

room.name: The Lost Orrery: Moonstairs
room.description: A stair of pale crescents climbs through hanging dust. Each step is heavier or lighter depending on whether you remember a promise kept.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Moonstairs Vows
object.description: Silver words float above the steps, naming debts owed by the Thorn Court to the wider Marches.
object.interact_text: You read the vows aloud. The stairs steady, and the Orrery admits the Thorn Court cannot survive the dead star alone.

room.name: The Lost Orrery: Starwell
room.description: A vertical well opens to an impossible sky. Stars hang close enough to touch, but each one carries a whisper of a future where Onfadell burns.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Near Stars
object.description: Tiny stars drift just beyond reach, arranged like a warning map.
object.interact_text: You mark the star-pattern in court ink. It confirms the Lost Orrery is one of the relic stations tied to the Astral Crown.

room.name: The Lost Orrery: Gearvault Below
room.description: Beneath the axis, sleeping gears fill a vault like bronze roots. Some are stamped with Onfadell heraldry; others bear symbols of Hearthwatch, Greenbarrow, and distant zones not yet visited.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Wardline Gears
object.description: The largest gear has a missing lens socket and a carved warning in Sylvan and old Common.
object.interact_text: You examine the missing socket. The Orrery can project the next relic route only after the Moonlit Orrery Lens is restored.

room.name: The Lost Orrery: Broken Planetarium
room.description: The dome above is cracked, yet its illusions still turn: root-moons, ghost-comets, the Crownless dark between planes, and a thorn-shaped constellation guarding a royal secret.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Broken Planetarium Projection
object.description: The projection stutters between ancient Onfadell and the present dead-star crisis.
object.interact_text: You fit the Moonlit Orrery Lens into the projection. A path appears from Onfadell to the Grotto of the Nameless Oracle, proving the Oracle is entangled with the main relic chain.

room.name: Grotto of the Nameless Oracle: Briar-Mouth
room.description: A cave opens beneath woven thorns behind the Thorn Court seat. No guard stands here; the entrance itself refuses to remember who last entered.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Briar-Mouth Silence
object.description: The entrance consumes titles, boasts, and family names, leaving only intent.
object.interact_text: You enter without declaring yourself. The grotto accepts humility but sharpens every hidden resentment nearby.

room.name: Grotto: Veilpool Antechamber
room.description: A shallow pool reflects everyone as they were before their first broken promise. Veils of hanging moss divide the chamber into soft green shadows.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Veilpool Reflection
object.description: The pool shows faces wearing names they abandoned.
object.interact_text: You watch the reflection without flinching. It reveals the Oracle’s revenge is aimed at every Fey who benefited from her erasure, innocent descendants included.

room.name: Grotto: Echoing Reeds
room.description: Tall reeds grow from stone cracks and speak in borrowed voices. Some repeat court testimony. Others repeat words that no living witness survived to hear.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Reed Testimony
object.description: A cluster of black reeds repeats one trial from many contradictory viewpoints.
object.interact_text: You listen until the contradictions align. The Oracle was condemned for telling a true prophecy the Court refused to pay for.

room.name: Grotto: Shelves of Unkept Memory
room.description: Stalactites hang like shelves, each holding droplets that contain erased memories. When a drop falls, someone in Onfadell forgets an old kindness.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Unkept Memory Drops
object.description: The droplets tremble with recollections too inconvenient for court records.
object.interact_text: You catch a falling memory in a glassroot charm. It preserves proof that the Nameless Oracle was betrayed by specific nobles, not all Fey folk.

room.name: Grotto: Three Springs of Judgment
room.description: Three springs feed the grotto: Truth, Grief, and Debt. None is hostile by itself, but together they form a trial no simple heroics can pass.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Three Springs Choice
object.description: The springs murmur in different moral languages: what happened, what it cost, and who still owes.
object.interact_text: You let all three speak before choosing action. The chamber opens the descent because you refuse the easy lie of blame without responsibility.

room.name: Grotto: Spring of Truth
room.description: Clear water pours over black stone inscribed with forbidden minutes from Thorn Court trials. The truth here is clean, cold, and completely uninterested in comfort.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Truthspring Minutes
object.description: The carved minutes name the first conspirators who stripped the Oracle of her name.
object.interact_text: You copy the names exactly. The guilt narrows from a people to a crime, weakening the Oracle’s indiscriminate vengeance.

room.name: Grotto: Spring of Grief
room.description: Silver water falls silently into a basin full of flower petals. Every petal is a mourning token for someone hurt by prophecy, politics, or both.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Griefspring Petals
object.description: The petals carry the names of people the Court failed and the Oracle now endangers.
object.interact_text: You gather the freshest petals. Their names remind the grotto that revenge creates new mourners faster than justice can name old ones.

room.name: Grotto: Spring of Debt
room.description: Amber water seeps from a crack in the stone and hardens into coins that cannot be spent. Each coin bears a favor unpaid by the Thorn Court.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Unspendable Debt Coins
object.description: The coins are too heavy for their size and warm with court shame.
object.interact_text: You weigh one coin against the Thorn Court writ. The debt becomes a vow of repair rather than fuel for the Oracle’s curse.

room.name: Grotto: Unspeaking Descent
room.description: The passage descends by denying language. Spoken words vanish as mist. Gestures, intentions, and old wounds become painfully clear.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Wordless Runes
object.description: Runes mark the wall without letters, meaning only what the reader has avoided saying.
object.interact_text: You read the runes as confession rather than command. The grotto stops reshaping the corridor around denial.

room.name: Grotto: Root-Mirror Chamber
room.description: Twisted roots form a mirror that reflects not bodies but loyalties. The Thorn Court appears as beauty and cruelty intertwined; the Oracle appears as pain given a throne.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Root-Mirror Loyalties
object.description: The mirror demands you identify the difference between defending the Fey and excusing the Court.
object.interact_text: You name the difference aloud. The mirror cracks open, revealing a path to the chamber where the Oracle keeps her stolen absence.

room.name: Grotto: Chamber of the Last Name
room.description: Here the cave walls are blank except for one erased place where a name should be. The air trembles with the outline of a person turned into a function: oracle, weapon, warning.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Erased Name Hollow
object.description: The hollow in the wall is shaped like a missing name and a wound that learned to speak.
object.interact_text: You set the name-fragments in order. The Oracle hesitates for the first time, forced to remember she was harmed before she became harm.

room.name: Grotto: Pool of All Stolen Names
room.description: The heart of the grotto is a round black pool filled with names stolen from Fey, mortals, beasts, rivers, and roads. The Nameless Oracle waits above it like a queen reflected in a blade.

companion_dialogue.line: The air is thick with old bargains. Speak carefully; even silence may be witnessed here.
Onfadell is not abandoned. It is listening from every branch and pane of green glass.

object.name: Pool of Stolen Names
object.description: Every ripple contains a life reduced to leverage. The relic rests below the water, guarded by revenge made sacred.
object.interact_text: You claim the Crownroot Thorn Sigil from the pool after the Oracle falls or yields. Onfadell’s relic joins the Marches by contested oath, not conquest.

room.name: Dawnhammer Roadhead
room.description: The road leaves Fey shadow behind and rises into hammer-colored hills. Survey stakes, caravan bells, dwarf-cut drainage channels, and warning cairns mark the border of the Dawnhammer Free State. No banner flies over the road; the locals say good steel does not need a crown.

companion_dialogue.line: These hills are not ruled by a court or crown. That may make them free, but it also makes every bargain matter.
Listen to the wagons. Empty axles heading east, loaded axles heading west. The rhythm is broken.

object.name: Free Road Markers
object.description: Three stone pillars name the local compact: no slave work, no faction monopoly, no mine sealed without witness.
object.interact_text: You read the compact and learn why the Crownless Cabal would rather conquer Dawnhammer than merely raid it.
object.completed_text: The Dawnhammer compact is already marked in your notes.

room.name: Switchback Watch
room.description: A low watchpost overlooks the sun-iron road. Dwarf roadwardens, human carters, and gnome signalers compare smoke codes while ravens circle a recent wreck below the red scree.

object.name: Signal Mirror
object.description: The mirror is aimed toward Vandarom, but dried blood darkens the adjustment wheel.
object.interact_text: You realign the mirror, restoring a safe signal between watchpost and city.
object.completed_text: The signal mirror is already sending bright hammer-code down the road.

room.name: Red Scree Ambush Site
room.description: Loose red stone slides underfoot around a burned wagon. The raiders struck from above, cut the trace chains, and left only the sun-iron samples they could not carry.

object.name: Ambush Ruts
object.description: Wheel ruts veer sharply toward a scrape in the hillside, too deliberate for ordinary bandits.
object.interact_text: You trace the ruts and find a branded chain-link stamped with the Crownless Cabal cipher.
object.completed_text: The ambush site has already given up its route.

room.name: Raider Hide-Scrape
room.description: A cramped scrape behind a curtain of gravel contains stolen harness rings, dwarf-made ration tins, and a fresh tunnel mark burned into the back wall.

room.name: Sun-Iron Way: Western Cut
room.description: The main trade route runs between stacked retaining walls. Ore wagons from Bhon Falduhr grind east while finished tool-carts from Vandarom clatter west, each crew pretending not to count the missing wagons.

object.name: Caravan Tally Posts
object.description: Iron nails mark each wagon that passed. Recent columns have gaps wide enough to frighten an accountant.
object.interact_text: You compare the tallies and confirm the raids target raw sun-iron, not coin or food.
object.completed_text: The tally discrepancy is already recorded.

room.name: Bhon Falduhr Mine Gate
room.description: Bhon Falduhr is cut into the hill behind a gate of black granite and brass counterweights. Every entering worker taps the lintel and names a living kinsperson before the bell admits them.

object.name: Gate Lintel Oath
object.description: The oath names free labor and safe return as equal duties.
object.interact_text: You repeat the visitor oath and earn cautious nods from the gate crew.
object.completed_text: The gate crew already recognizes your oath.

room.name: Bhon Falduhr Yard
room.description: Cranes swing ore baskets over sorting tables while miners argue over seam quality, lunch quality, and whose cousin invented the better rivet. The site feels worried, not broken.

room.name: Bhon Falduhr Assay Hall
room.description: Blue flame licks beneath crucibles as assayers test ore for sun-iron purity. Slates show output falling despite rich seams, a contradiction that has the miners whispering about stolen shifts.

object.name: Assay Slates
object.description: The numbers prove the mine is producing enough ore; the loss happens after extraction.
object.interact_text: You audit the slates and isolate the missing lots by shift bell, narrowing the raid window.
object.completed_text: The assay evidence is already copied.

room.name: Bhon Falduhr: Sun-Iron Face
room.description: A living seam of sun-iron glows through drilled stone, warm as dawn through church glass. Miners work in pairs so no one disappears quietly.

object.name: Sun-Iron Face Sample
object.description: A loose vein chip hums with stored daylight.
object.interact_text: You collect a lawful sample that can identify forged shipments and Cabal counterfeits.
object.completed_text: You already have a legitimate sun-iron sample.

room.name: Bhon Falduhr: Sealed Old Gallery
room.description: Old support arches vanish into colder stone. The miners bricked this gallery after three bells rang from below without hands to pull them.

room.name: Bhon Falduhr Lift House
room.description: Massive gears lower ore cages through the mountain. A brass plate lists every mechanic who ever improved the lift, with blank space left for apprentices not born yet.

room.name: Bhon Falduhr Deep Lift
room.description: The cage drops through damp heat, old names, and the smell of oil. Halfway down, a side gate has been forced open from the abandoned tunnels.

room.name: Bhon Falduhr Bunkhouse
room.description: Boots dry beneath iron beds, tin mugs hang from numbered hooks, and exhausted miners keep one eye on the door. The missing shifts have turned sleep into another workplace hazard.

room.name: Bhon Falduhr Counting Office
room.description: Ledgers, shift bells, route maps, and sealed pay-chits fill a windowless office guarded more fiercely than the ore yard. The books show a theft pattern, but not a thief.

object.name: Counting Ledger
object.description: The shipment numbers are clean until the wagons reach the middle road.
object.interact_text: You copy the missing wagon marks and reveal that the raiders know the private shift schedule.
object.completed_text: The stolen shift pattern is already identified.

room.name: Sun-Iron Way: Midway Stones
room.description: Granite distance stones stand between mine and city. Campfires burn at all hours because wagons now travel in tight convoys rather than in the old confident trickle.

room.name: Convoy Cookfires
room.description: A temporary camp of halfling cooks, dwarf guards, elven wheelwrights, and tired oxen has grown around the midway stones. Everyone has a theory, and every theory smells of smoke.

room.name: Broken Wagon Hollow
room.description: A hollow below the main road is littered with shattered spokes, snapped brake pins, and one wagon bed dragged toward the abandoned mine mouth. The raid was organized like a military seizure, not a robbery.

object.name: Broken Axle Marks
object.description: The axles were cut with cold necromantic pressure, preserving the wood fibers in a dead curl.
object.interact_text: You identify the sabotage method and prove the raiders have arcane support.
object.completed_text: The sabotage method is already known.

room.name: Abandoned Wheelwright Shack
room.description: The shack once repaired caravan wheels; now its walls are scored with chain measurements and crude diagrams of dwarf shackles.

room.name: Sun-Iron Way: Eastern Grade
room.description: The road climbs toward Vandarom in engineered terraces. Finished plowshares, hinges, saws, and sword blanks move west under guard, proof that the dwarves make for more than war.

object.name: Terrace Lanterns
object.description: Several road lanterns have been doused with grave-wax.
object.interact_text: You scrape away the wax and relight the lanterns, restoring the caravan night route.
object.completed_text: The eastern grade lanterns already burn clean.

room.name: Vandarom West Gate
room.description: The manufacturing city of Vandarom rises in stepped brass balconies, smoke filters, and hammer towers. The gate guards inspect manifests more carefully than faces.

object.name: Manifest Gate
object.description: Every cart entering Vandarom must show buyer, metal grade, and intended use.
object.interact_text: You review recent manifests and see no legal buyer for the stolen sun-iron.
object.completed_text: The Vandarom manifests are already reviewed.

room.name: Vandarom Guildhall
room.description: The guildhall is a domed civic forge where mining crews, smelters, engineers, carters, armorers, and foreign buyers negotiate beneath a rule hammered into the floor: labor is not property.

room.name: Vandarom Foundry Quarter
room.description: Hammer towers strike in staggered rhythm while molten sun-iron pours through warded channels. The quarter can build plows, hinges, surgical tools, or blades; the buyer decides whether steel becomes life or tyranny.

room.name: Vandarom Gear Market
room.description: Market stalls sell rivets by the handful, lantern cages by the dozen, and arguments for free. Dwarves dominate the counters, but the buyers represent nearly every road in the Marches.

room.name: Vandarom Caravan Yard
room.description: Loaded wagons wait under numbered cranes while caravan families sleep beside their teams. The yard should sound like commerce; lately it sounds like counting casualties.

room.name: Vandarom Rune Press
room.description: A vertical workshop stamps maker marks, safety runes, and buyer seals into hot metal. The press refuses to stamp chain-links after the old liberation wars.

object.name: Rune Press Jam
object.description: A shard of black sigil-bone is wedged in the press teeth.
object.interact_text: You remove the sigil-bone and prove someone tried to counterfeit a Dawnhammer maker mark for Cabal weapons.
object.completed_text: The rune press already works cleanly.

room.name: The Open Anvil Taproom
room.description: A public house built around an unused anvil where any worker may speak grievances without a foreman interrupting. Travelers trade songs beside dwarf shift crews and nervous foreign buyers.

room.name: The Quiet Tunnels: Abandoned Mouth
room.description: The old mine mouth gapes below the trade road. No wind exits, no water drips, and no animal nests along the sill. The silence is too complete for stone.

companion_dialogue.line: Mines should answer with echoes, carts, chain, water, something. This place is holding its breath.
Watch the floor. Abandoned workings kill even when nothing evil is helping them.

object.name: Rotten Warning Boards
object.description: Old boards warn of blind raises, bad air, and flooded sumps. Newer Cabal marks point slave crews inward.
object.interact_text: You copy the old mine warnings and gain enough layout sense to spot several dead-end cuts.
object.completed_text: The Quiet Tunnels warnings are already copied.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Foreman Station
room.description: A collapsed desk, dented helmet hooks, and a shift board mark the first station. Cabal chalk has overwritten the safety routes with quotas for prisoners not yet captured.

object.name: Overwritten Shift Board
object.description: The old worker names are crossed out and replaced with numbers, exactly what Dawnhammer law forbids.
object.interact_text: You preserve the board as evidence that the Cabal plans enslavement, not banditry.
object.completed_text: The shift board evidence is already preserved.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Dead-End Timber Pocket
room.description: The tunnel ends at a wall of old timbers bowed like ribs. Someone hid supplies here before abandoning the mine, and no Cabal boot has searched low enough.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Ore Cart Spur
room.description: Twisted rails split into several narrow cuts. Cart numbers painted on the wall contradict the actual tracks, a deliberate confusion made worse by decades of collapse.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: False Vein Dead End
room.description: Fool's shine glitters across a wall that never held sun-iron. The dead end exists because someone once chased a lie into stone.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Pitfall Drop
room.description: The floor gives way into a support void. Broken ladders, smashed helmets, and a cold draft show this pit has swallowed both miners and raiders.

object.name: Broken Pit Ladder
object.description: The ladder is cracked but can be braced with loose rail spikes.
object.interact_text: You brace the ladder enough to make the pit a risky shortcut instead of a trap.
object.completed_text: The pit ladder is already braced.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Dry Powder Cache
room.description: A sealed side chamber still holds old blasting powder in waxed kegs. A careless spark would bring half the tunnel down, which explains why the Cabal left guards instead of looters.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Sunken Rail Junction
room.description: Rails sink into black water at a four-way junction. The safe path is not the straight one; the straight one is how miners drowned when the pumps died.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Side-Cutter Cache
room.description: A low crawlway opens into a surveyor's cache. The side-cutters who made it hid practical tools for anyone sensible enough to distrust the main tunnel.

object.name: Side-Cutter Lockbox
object.description: A rugged lockbox bears a wheelwright's stamp.
object.missing_item_text: The lockbox requires the side-cutter cache key from the abandoned wheelwright shack.
object.interact_text: You open the lockbox and recover a careful map of the side cuts.
object.completed_text: The side-cutter lockbox is already open.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Pump Sump
room.description: Cold water laps against silent pump wheels. The old machinery is dwarf-made and stubborn, but necromantic residue clogs the intake valves like black moss.

object.name: Clogged Pump Wheels
object.description: Necromantic clots have jammed the pump vanes.
object.interact_text: You clear the pump vanes. Water begins draining from the lower workings with a groan like a waking beast.
object.completed_text: The sump pumps already churn in slow, clean rhythm.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Collapsed Barricade
room.description: A barricade of cart bodies, broken braces, and old lunch pails blocks the original haul road. Someone died trying to keep the lower mine sealed.

object.name: Barricade Names
object.description: Names are scratched inside the cart boards where only trapped miners would have seen them.
object.interact_text: You record the names and restore them to the living ledger of Bhon Falduhr.
object.completed_text: The barricade names are already recorded.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Unfinished Chain Pens
room.description: Fresh iron rings are drilled into the stone, sized for wrists and ankles rather than cargo. The Cabal has not yet filled the pens, but the shackles prove what they intended for Dawnhammer.

object.name: Unfinished Shackles
object.description: The shackles are new, ugly, and mass-produced from stolen sun-iron.
object.interact_text: You break the chain fixtures and ruin the Cabal's ready-made prison.
object.completed_text: The chain pens are already broken beyond use.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Lower Haulage
room.description: The lower haulage road runs wide enough for three ore carts, then narrows without warning. Every side cut offers either a cache, a corpse, or a fall.

companion_dialogue.line: This mine does not branch like a dungeon. It branches like work interrupted by death.
The useful supplies are not on the main route. Miners hid them where only patient travelers would look.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Echo Chamber
room.description: Every footstep returns from the wrong angle. Old survey marks warn that this chamber makes tunnels sound open even when they end in solid stone.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Hidden Audit Cache
room.description: A narrow chamber holds duplicate ledgers, spare candles, and a bottle of brandy labeled for emergencies involving auditors or cave-ins.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Blind Raise
room.description: A vertical shaft climbs into darkness and stops against a collapsed ceiling. Dust falls whenever the mountain remembers gravity.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Bone-Rail Tram
room.description: A short tram line has been rebuilt with bones lashed to iron like sleepers. Dead miners push empty carts in circles until a Cabal bell tells them otherwise.

object.name: Bone-Rail Brake Pin
object.description: A black iron pin controls the tram's necromantic loop.
object.interact_text: You wrench the pin free, and the bone-rail tram crashes silent against the far wall.
object.completed_text: The bone-rail tram is already disabled.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Crownless Forge Plan
room.description: Tables display weapon schematics for spearheads, chain hooks, siege rivets, and slave collars. Every design bears a false Vandarom maker mark.

object.name: Cabal Forge Schematics
object.description: The schematics show how stolen sun-iron would arm only the Crownless Cabal.
object.interact_text: You gather the forge plans before the ink can crawl off the page.
object.completed_text: The Cabal forge plans are already secured.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Black Anvil Chapel
room.description: The Cabal has turned an old break room into a chapel of coerced labor. A black anvil sits where the miners once kept soup pots, drinking ghost-light from the helmets nailed above it.

object.name: Black Anvil
object.description: The anvil binds miner remains into unwilling labor.
object.interact_text: You crack the binding rune and the chamber fills with one long relieved exhale.
object.completed_text: The black anvil is already cracked and powerless.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Sun-Iron Reliquary
room.description: A sealed pocket of clean sun-iron survived beneath a miner's prayer wheel. Its light does not brighten the room; it clarifies it, showing every forced chain as an obscenity.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Lichlit Stoping
room.description: Here the mine has been widened by magic rather than tools. The walls shine with corpse-pale light, and every foothold looks trustworthy until it is not.

room.name: Quiet Tunnels: Collapsed Stope Dead End
room.description: The stoping ends in a tilted chamber where ore pockets have been ripped out like teeth. A small cache survives behind a fallen drill frame.

room.name: The Quiet Tunnels: Blackvein Command Vault
room.description: A vault chamber has been cleared into a command post for forced manufacture. Bone miners stand at attention around cold forges while Master Veskar Blackvein, a necromancer in cracked sun-iron mail, writes production orders for an army that has no living workers.

companion_dialogue.line: This is the opposite of Dawnhammer: craft without consent, labor without wages, steel without conscience.
End him here, or every free forge in these hills becomes a chain factory.

object.name: Blackvein Command Table
object.description: The command table lists quotas for weapons, slave collars, and siege hinges meant only for the Crownless Cabal.
object.interact_text: You seize the command orders and the Dawn-Forge Keystone flares, joining the Marches relic chain.
object.completed_text: The command orders and keystone have already been secured.

room.name: Sunken Crown Marsh: Blackwater Approach
room.description: The road from Dawnhammer breaks into plank causeways, reed-skiff posts, and warning stakes carved with Draconic teeth-marks. The air smells of peat, warm rain, and old stone drowned below living marsh.

companion_dialogue.line: The marsh is not empty. It is watching from under every lily pad.
Those warning stakes look newer than the ruins. The living have stronger claims than the dead.

room.name: Blackwater Lotus Isle
room.description: A low island of medicinal lotus blooms around half-submerged marble steps. Lizardfolk gathering marks show which flowers may be cut and which are left for the brood pools.

room.name: Blackwater Causeway
room.description: Wobbly planks cross black water between drowned milestones. Beneath the surface, the walls of an ancient road continue straight toward a keep that sank before the lizardfolk claimed the marsh.

room.name: Drowned Cause-Stones
room.description: Old royal cause-stones protrude from the mire like broken teeth. Each stone has been overwritten with Hawga Daar scratch-runes warning outsiders not to confuse ruins with ownership.

room.name: Ghost Barge Mooring
room.description: A rotted cargo barge rests where no current could have carried it. When mist crosses the deck, a poleman appears and counts passengers who are not there.

room.name: Ghost Barge Hold
room.description: The hold is packed with sealed jars, wet rope, and royal tax ledgers whose ink re-forms after every drop of water. Not all cargo here was ever meant to be unloaded.

room.name: Reed-Blind Watch
room.description: A lizardfolk blind hides in cattails above the causeway. Silent watchers track every outsider by wake pattern, scent, and whether they reach for steel before speaking.

room.name: Mire Hunter Camp
room.description: Skinned crocodile hide stretches over poles, and spear racks face the open water. This is not a friendly camp, but every knot and cookfire shows discipline rather than savagery.

room.name: Mangrove Cut
room.description: Mangrove roots arch over a tight waterway where skiffs scrape through single-file. Bits of old battlement stone have been woven into living root walls.

room.name: Trial Pool of Patient Teeth
room.description: A circular pool is fenced with reed charms, bite-scarred shields, and polished shells. Hawga Daar uses this place for proving hunts, not entertainment.

room.name: Hatchling Reed-Nest
room.description: Warm reed bundles line a sheltered mudbank. Tiny claw marks in the silt show where hatchlings were recently moved in a hurry.

room.name: Blackjaw Den
room.description: A cramped den under exposed roots stinks of wet scales and stolen offerings. Something large has dragged brood-shells here and guarded them with territorial patience.

room.name: Hawga Daar Outer Palings
room.description: Sharpened cypress palings rise from the mud before a village of stilt-houses and half-drowned royal walls. The gate remains shut until the clan decides an outsider is less dangerous inside than outside.

room.name: Hawga Daar Heartwalk
room.description: The true village opens on a raised lattice of cypress walkways. Stilt homes lean over old stone roofs, and cooking smoke rises from chimneys that were once watchtower vents.
room.locked_message: The gate-speaker lowers a reed spear across the walkway. Hawga Daar village proper is closed until Ssharketh grants you the Hawga Daar Oath-Scale.

companion_dialogue.line: This is a village built on top of a graveyard and still very much alive.
They are not guarding treasure first. They are guarding children.

room.name: Brood-Mother’s Platform
room.description: A broad platform circles a sunken watchtower crown. Ssharketh receives disputes here with no throne, no crown, and no patience for outsiders who mistake either absence for weakness.

room.name: Warm-Nest Broodhouse
room.description: Clay heat-stones, reed curtains, and old royal floor mosaics keep the broodhouse warm. Hatchlings sleep where a forgotten king’s courtiers once waited to flatter him.

room.name: Stilt-House Ring
room.description: Family houses stand on tall stilts over clean channels. Nets dry beside carved ancestor poles, and every ladder can be pulled up faster than an invader can cross the mud.

room.name: Bonecarver Dock
room.description: The dock is strung with polished bone hooks, cypress spearshafts, and charms made from creatures that lost arguments with Hawga Daar hunters.

room.name: Story Stones of Hawga Daar
room.description: Sunken blocks from the lost keep have been raised into a circle and carved with lizardfolk memory marks. Oral history and old masonry argue here without needing translators.

room.name: Pumpwright Pier
room.description: Bronze pump parts hang from poles above tidy tool mats. Hawga Daar keeps the ancient mechanisms running selectively, draining only what the clan chooses to remember.

room.name: Sunken Plaza of the Lost King
room.description: A drowned royal plaza lies beneath knee-deep water, now used for clan rites. The lizardfolk name Hawga Daar means Lost King, but their ceremonies honor survival rather than monarchy.

room.name: Ruin-Market Under Stilt Shadows
room.description: Trade mats cover the roof of an old basilica. Fish, bronze fittings, herbs, bonework, salvaged masonry, and suspiciously watched outsider goods change hands under low awnings.

room.name: Old Keep Overlook
room.description: From the village edge, the old keep rises from the marsh like a drowned knuckle. Water spills through arrow slits, and something below tolls a bell without sound.

room.name: The Sunken Vaults: Drowned Sallyport
room.description: The entrance to the old keep sits below a leaning arch of royal stone and lizardfolk warning totems. A stair descends through green water toward vaults that were sealed before the marsh learned their names.

room.name: Old Keep Courtyard
room.description: The courtyard is a marsh basin full of toppled statues, stilted scout platforms, and drowned training circles. Every step alternates between stone, mud, and water deep enough to hide a hand.

room.name: Gatehouse Dead-End Cache
room.description: The old gatehouse has collapsed into a blind room behind a rusted portcullis. Someone hid supplies here during the last hours of the kingdom and never returned for them.

room.name: Cracked Battlement Walk
room.description: A narrow battlement leans over the marsh. From here the player can see Hawga Daar’s stilt houses deliberately avoiding the keep’s central tower, as if the village refuses to stand beneath old authority.

room.name: Cistern Works: Upper Pump House
room.description: The first pump room smells of algae, bronze, and long neglect. Chains run down into the vault, but one great wheel hangs motionless until the missing crank is fitted.

object.name: Upper Sluice Pump
object.description: A bronze pump-wheel waits beside a socket shaped for Drokh’s restored crank.
object.missing_item_text: The pump cannot be turned without the restored Vault Pump Crank from Hawga Daar.
object.interact_text: You fit the crank and force the wheel through three grinding turns. Somewhere below, trapped water roars into a drainage shaft.
object.completed_text: The upper pump is already moving in slow, stubborn circles.

room.name: Upper Drain Spillway
room.description: Recently drained water still pours through this spillway in violent sheets. The path is loud, slick, and optional, but it bypasses several flooded passages for players willing to explore the pump works.

room.name: Sunken Vaults: Floodline Anteroom
room.description: The anteroom bears three distinct waterlines: the flood that killed the garrison, the flood that buried the kingdom, and the fresh line now dropping by inches. Crown mosaics vanish under black water to the north.

room.name: Silted Records Room
room.description: Wax tablets, ledger bones, and drowned contract cylinders lie under silt. The records suggest the lost kingdom pledged one band of a celestial crown as a military safeguard, then hid the pledge from its own people.

room.name: Drained Armory
room.description: This armory becomes reachable only after the upper pump lowers the water. Racks of old spears stand in mud, and a sluice key hangs from the skeletal wrist of an officer who refused to abandon his post.

room.name: Knee-Deep Gallery
room.description: The corridor slopes unevenly, forcing the player to wade past arrow slits that now pour steady curtains of water. Alcoves lead nowhere except to drowned boots and snapped spearshafts.

room.name: Half-Drowned Barracks
room.description: Bunk frames jut from water like rib bones. Most side doors are swollen shut, but a broken latrine shaft drops into darkness for anyone reckless enough to test old floors.

room.name: Pitfall Shaft
room.description: The floor gives way into a vertical maintenance shaft. It is a punishing detour rather than a shortcut, but old repair niches hide small valuables for careful climbers.

room.name: Sump Dead-End Cache
room.description: The lowest sump is a blind pocket of foul air, cold water, and lost tools. A waterproof coffer has been wedged above the scum line by someone who expected to climb back out.

room.name: Pumped-Out Prison Cells
room.description: Only after the upper pump runs can these cells be entered without swimming blind. Prison marks on the walls show that the lost kingdom jailed debtors, rebels, and lizardfolk scouts long before the marsh took its revenge.

room.name: Lower Pump Chamber
room.description: A second pump chamber waits behind knee-deep water and silt-clogged gears. This mechanism controls the deeper vault, but its sluice lock has been sealed with royal authority.

object.name: Lower Sluice Pump
object.description: A locked pump lever bears the lost kingdom’s crown mark, almost scratched away by lizardfolk claws.
object.missing_item_text: The lower pump lever is locked. The Sluice Gate Key should be somewhere in the drained armory or gatehouse remains.
object.interact_text: You turn the key and haul the lever down. The lower vault answers with a thunderous gulp as black water drains below the mosaic hall.
object.completed_text: The lower sluice remains open, and the deeper vault keeps breathing out damp air.

room.name: Crown Mosaic Hall
room.description: The hall’s floor mosaic depicts a radiant crown divided into bands and set beneath constellations. One band has been pried from the image, but its outline matches the dead-star geometry seen in the Lost Orrery.

room.name: Chain-Pulley Dead End
room.description: Chains vanish into a collapsed lift shaft. The route is a dead end, but the counterweight housing hides a maintenance cache above the floodline.

room.name: Pumped-Out Sunken Treasury
room.description: When the lower pump succeeds, this treasury emerges from black water with a sigh of trapped air. Coins remain, but the more important absence is crown-shaped.

room.name: Oath-Shield Grotto
room.description: Natural limestone has broken through worked stone, forming a grotto where shields hang from roots like drowned fruit. Each shield bears the same vow: Guard the Crown Until the King Returns.

room.name: Knight-Captain’s Watch
room.description: A dry landing overlooks the final vault. Wight-squires stand in alcoves with lowered heads, waiting for the captain to name another enemy of a kingdom that no longer exists.

room.name: The Sunken Vaults: Drowned Oathhall
room.description: The deepest oathhall is drained just enough for battle. Captain Ildran Veyr stands before a broken crown reliquary, convinced that Hawga Daar, the Fey, the Marches, and every living heir are usurpers. The Drowned Band of the Astral Crown burns cold in his breastplate.

room.name: Buried Titan Highway: Marshward Gate
room.description: The Sunken Crown Marsh ends at a raised causeway where black mud gives way to amber glass-sand. Ahead, the Buried Titan Highway runs east across the Expanse, its paving stones interrupted by enormous ribs of pale stone that nomads insist are the bones of a dead giant.

object.name: Titan Gate Marker
object.description: A half-buried milestone shows a giant hand holding three mirrors.
object.interact_text: You copy the milestone marks and note that each mirror points toward a different tower line.
object.completed_text: The titan gate marker has already been copied into your notes.

room.name: Buried Titan Highway: Stone-Rib Mile
room.description: The highway climbs over a ridge of white stone ribs large enough to shelter wagons in their shadows. Blue Veil caravans leave colored knots on iron pegs to warn of raiders, weather, and rival research teams.

room.name: Buried Titan Finger Cache
room.description: A fossilized finger-bone rises from the sand like a fallen column. Beneath its knuckle, old caravaneers hid water, spell components, and warnings no formal map admits.

room.name: Buried Titan Highway: Mirage Well
room.description: A circular well stands in the center of the highway, though its water appears ten paces away from wherever one looks. Ajuna chalk, Dhanor brass pins, and Shakni silence knots compete for space on the same weathered stones.

room.name: Saltflat Raid Site
room.description: Broken wheel rims, scorched canvas, and dotted lines of blood mark a caravan ambush carried out in impossible noon-brightness. The raiders knew exactly when the tower mirrors would blind the highway.
