room.name: Veilglass Sink
room.description: The desert drops into a bowl of translucent sand that hums with half-heard notes. Footprints appear before feet make them, then sink away as if embarrassed.

room.name: Buried Titan Highway: Dhanor Turn
room.description: Heavy caravan ruts branch south toward brass tents and repair cranes. The main road continues east, lined with mirrored warning flags that flash in patterns only trained caravaners can read.

room.name: Buried Titan Highway: Titan-Spine Causeway
room.description: A long raised ridge carries the road over a low dune sea. The stones are warm even at night, and every caravan animal lowers its head here as if passing a grave.

room.name: Sunblistered Waystone
room.description: A cracked waystone leans in a field of heat-shattered glass. Someone has carved equations over older prayers, then scratched warnings through both.

room.name: Buried Titan Highway: Shakni Turn
room.description: White cloth pennants mark the turn toward the Shakni camp. The highway itself continues east into a dead-still basin where even the wind seems to avoid trespassing.

room.name: Buried Titan Highway: Invisible Barrier Basin
room.description: The road enters a shallow basin and simply stops casting a shadow. Caravans go around this place. Scholars stare at it until headaches make them religious.

object.name: Triune Mirage Alignment
object.description: Three mirrorless posts stand in a triangle, each waiting for a tower angle to agree with the other two.
object.missing_item_text: The posts refuse to focus. You need the Triune Mirage Index created from the three tower readings.
object.interact_text: You set the Triune Mirage Index between the posts. The basin folds outward, revealing a doorway made of missing light.
object.completed_text: The Invisible Dungeon’s barrier already hangs open like a wound in the horizon.

room.name: Buried Titan Highway: Eastern Arch of Blue Veils
room.description: An arch of wind-carved stone marks the eastern edge of the Expanse. Blue ribbons snap from its hooks, each one bearing the name of a caravan that crossed the glass sands and lived.

room.name: Ajuna Camp: Starcloth Gate
room.description: Blue and copper awnings form a crescent around camel lines, chalk circles, and starcloth screens. Ajuna children chase mirage moths through equations drawn in sand.

room.name: Ajuna Camp: Starcloth Pavilion
room.description: The Ajuna head pavilion hangs from poles that never cast the same shadow twice. Research boards display wind formulae, spell routes, and polite insults aimed at Dhanor lens theory.

room.name: Ajuna Camp: Lens Yard
room.description: Apprentices turn hand mirrors by finger-width increments while Saffi tests whether heat can be persuaded to walk around a person instead of through them.

room.name: Ajuna Camp: Guest Mat Circle
room.description: A ring of carpets, cushions, and low tea tables receives outsiders. Every conversation is hospitality, interview, and research trial at once.

room.name: Ajuna Camp: Formula Scroll Wagon
room.description: A wagon of cedar drawers and blue glass lamps holds field-safe spells copied onto treated vellum. Dangerous originals are chained under the floorboards.

room.name: Dhanor Camp: Brass Yard
room.description: The Dhanor camp is all tool-noise, lens cranes, folding anvils, guarded crates, and sun-iron fasteners traded from Dawnhammer caravans. No canvas flap hangs without a clever hinge.

room.name: Dhanor Camp: Brass-Eye Workshop
room.description: Lenses hang from rack arms like captured moons. Borun’s workbench contains a half-disassembled mirage mirror and three separate locks on the same biscuit tin.

room.name: Dhanor Camp: Map Tent
room.description: Waxed maps cover every surface, including the ceiling. Red pins mark supply raids. Blue pins mark research opportunities. Black pins mark places where both happened at once.

room.name: Dhanor Camp: Caravan Corral
room.description: Mules, beetle-carts, camel teams, and wheeled lens-cradles crowd the corral. Guards argue over which scratches came from raiders and which came from careless loading.

room.name: Dhanor Camp: Blue Pot Teahouse
room.description: The teahouse occupies the raised back of a wagon. Scholars from rival camps pretend to stop here for tea rather than information.

room.name: Shakni Camp: Ring of White Cloth
room.description: White tents form a ring around a windless center. The Shakni use bells, knots, glances, and sandclock turns to discuss theories without giving the desert too many words to steal.

room.name: Shakni Camp: Silent Library
room.description: Scrolls hang inside sealed glass tubes. Readers turn pages with bone tongs, and every shelf is warded against careless speech.

room.name: Shakni Camp: Glassflute Tents
room.description: The tents are full of flutes, tuning bowls, and measured silences. Some notes are written as tiny holes in white paper rather than marks of ink.

room.name: Shakni Camp: Sandclock Stage
room.description: A small stage of white lacquered boards hosts silent debates and spell demonstrations timed by elaborate sandclocks.

room.name: Azure Mirage Tower: Blue Base
room.description: The first mirror tower rises from a blue-glass dune, its base etched with Ajuna wind formulae and older titan marks. The stair appears to lean away from anyone who looks directly at it.

room.name: Azure Mirage Tower: Lens Stair
room.description: Curved steps climb between suspended lenses that show the same desert at different hours. One lens shows the dead star hanging low over the eastern basin.

room.name: Azure Mirage Tower: Mirror Deck
room.description: The top deck holds a circular mirror of blue glass. When aligned, it shows the Invisible Dungeon as a black doorway reflected in daylight.

object.name: Azure Mirage Mirror
object.description: A huge blue mirror waits on a swivel ring covered in Ajuna numbers.
object.interact_text: You turn the mirror until its reflection catches the barrier basin and marks the first alignment angle.
object.completed_text: The Azure Mirage Mirror remains aligned toward the invisible door.

room.name: Ember Mirage Tower: Brass Base
room.description: The second tower is braced with Dhanor brass ribs and warning plaques. Someone has recently forced the lower hatch and then carefully repaired it to hide the damage.

room.name: Ember Mirage Tower: Scriptorium
room.description: Long desks curve around a central heat lens. The scriptorium smells of hot ink, machine oil, and secrets hidden by people too proud to use ordinary locks.

object.name: Scuffed Sandglass Note
object.description: A note has been stepped on beside a desk: “When brass forgets, SANDGLASS remembers.”
object.interact_text: You smooth the note and copy the word SANDGLASS into your field journal.
object.completed_text: The password clue has already been recorded.

object.name: Sandglass Password Door
object.description: A narrow door is hidden behind stacked lens cases. Its lock face shows two glass bulbs pouring sand upward.
object.password_text: You speak SANDGLASS. The lock reverses its sand and opens the hidden cache.
object.password_failed_text: The glass bulbs spin once, then refuse the answer.
object.interact_text: The sand in the lock falls upward as you speak SANDGLASS. A cache door slides inward without a sound.
object.completed_text: The Sandglass Door already stands open behind the lens cases.

room.name: Ember Mirage Tower: Hidden Spell Cache
room.description: A cramped hidden chamber contains forbidden Dhanor drafts, revised ward diagrams, and one codex wrapped in mirrored leather.

room.name: Ember Mirage Tower: Mirror Deck
room.description: The tower deck holds an ember-colored mirror with brass focusing arms. Aligning it requires hand strength, patience, and several impolite Dhanor margin notes.

object.name: Ember Mirage Mirror
object.description: An ember mirror sits inside a cage of brass measurement arms.
object.interact_text: You crank the brass arms into position and record the second alignment angle.
object.completed_text: The Ember Mirage Mirror remains locked into its measured position.

room.name: Ivory Mirage Tower: Silent Base
room.description: The third tower is nearly white, and every footstep near it sounds far away. Shakni warning knots hang from bone pegs around the base.

room.name: Ivory Mirage Tower: Whisper Stair
room.description: The stairwell swallows speech. Etched instructions advise climbers to think in complete sentences and avoid humming.

room.name: Ivory Mirage Tower: Mirror Deck
room.description: A white mirror faces the silent horizon. It reflects no faces, only promises kept and promises rehearsed.

object.name: Ivory Mirage Mirror
object.description: The ivory mirror rests on a ring inscribed with silent vowel marks.
object.interact_text: You align the mirror without speaking. A thin white line appears across the barrier basin in the distance.
object.completed_text: The Ivory Mirage Mirror remains aligned in ritual silence.

room.name: Invisible Dungeon: Absent Threshold
room.description: The barrier opens into a doorway no eyes can hold. Sand blows around the threshold but never through it, sketching an entryway made of absence.

room.name: Invisible Dungeon: Unseen Foyer
room.description: The foyer is discovered by sound before sight: boot echoes, dripping spellglass, and the scrape of scales somewhere beyond the walls. Every torch flame bends toward the same empty corner.

room.name: Invisible Dungeon: Absent Wall Gallery
room.description: Paintings hang on walls that are not visible until dust settles against them. Each frame shows a Blue Veil camp being watched by an unseen eye.

room.name: Invisible Dungeon: Null-Sun Chamber
room.description: A black disk burns overhead without heat. Broken collars lie in rows beneath it, each fitted for a spellcaster’s throat.

room.name: Invisible Dungeon: Whisperless Kennel
room.description: Glass cages line the chamber, most empty, some holding claw marks made from inside and outside at once. The Glass Wyrm’s smaller spawn once slept here.

room.name: Invisible Dungeon: Hall of Wrong Shadows
room.description: The floor is bright, but the shadows point upward. Anyone standing still too long begins to hear their own footsteps arriving from the next room.

room.name: Invisible Dungeon: Prism Bath
room.description: A dry bath of glass dust lies beneath both the null-sun chamber and the hall of wrong shadows. Old researchers used it to reveal invisible structures, but the dust now clings to lungs and memories.

room.name: Invisible Dungeon: Refracted Crossing
room.description: Four corridors meet around a pillar that reflects everyone except the person looking at it. The correct path changes depending on which camp’s theory one trusts.

room.name: Invisible Dungeon: Room of Cartographers Who Lied
room.description: Map tables float at knee height, covered in blank vellum. Shadows crossing the vellum reveal corridors that the visible walls deny.

room.name: Invisible Dungeon: Glass-Bone Roost
room.description: Curved ribs of transparent bone arc overhead. The Glass Wyrm has shed teeth here, each one humming with devoured spellwork.

room.name: Invisible Dungeon: Shed-Skin Cache
room.description: A chamber half-filled with translucent shed skin curls around an old Blue Veil supply chest. Someone reached this far, hid their findings, and chose not to continue.

room.name: Invisible Dungeon: Upside-Down Stairs
room.description: The stairs climb to a ceiling, then continue as if gravity signed the wrong contract. From the top, the Glass Wyrm’s lair can be heard below and seen above.

room.name: Invisible Dungeon: Glass Wyrm’s Crucible
room.description: A vast circular hollow opens inside the invisible dungeon. The Glass Wyrm coils through walls as if they were water, its body full of swallowed spell diagrams and one cold shard of the Astral Crown’s concealment lens.

object.name: Mirage Crown Lens Pedestal
object.description: A cracked pedestal waits for the shard once the Glass Wyrm falls. Its inscriptions match the hidden roads shown by the dead star.
object.interact_text: You place the Mirage Shard against the pedestal long enough to read its ward-name: Concealment Without Exile.
object.completed_text: The pedestal has already yielded the Astral Crown lens-name.

room.name: Duskfall Coast: Saltflat Border Road
room.description: The heat of Glasswind gives way to salt wind, purple cloudbanks, and gulls circling above the Thesmeda Sea. A Tidebound stone marker warns that Terrecester Wharf is under pirate pressure but still taking lawful travelers.

object.name: Tidebound Boundary Marker
object.description: The marker is carved with a wave, a hooked knife, and a ferry bell.
object.interact_text: You learn the local law: no ferry passage without a Terrecester-stamped ticket, and no privateering without League bond.
object.completed_text: The boundary law has already been recorded.

room.name: Burnt Caravan Pullout
room.description: A supply wagon lies half-buried in wet sand. Kobold footprints scatter between powder burns, snapped harness, and crates marked for the Terrecester sea wall.

room.name: Tidebound League Checkpoint
room.description: A timber gatehouse spans the coast road. League guards inspect caravan seals under flapping blue pennants while refugees trade rumors about pirate sails offshore.

room.name: Gullwatch Bluff
room.description: A windswept bluff overlooks the coast road and the pale line of the Glendes Islands. Signal flags hang cut and retied in the wrong order.

room.name: Smuggler’s Step Path
room.description: A narrow stair has been chipped into the cliff by people who dislike customs houses. It descends to a pocket beach where shallow boats can hide beneath kelp nets.

room.name: Hidden Kelp Beach
room.description: Long kelp ropes curtain a black-sand beach. Someone has stacked casks of powder and dried fish under a canvas painted to look like rock.

room.name: Smuggler Reed-Ditch
room.description: A ditch of brackish water cuts through the reeds east of the checkpoint. Bootprints and clawed kobold tracks meet here, then vanish under floating boards.

room.name: Saltmarsh Boardwalk
room.description: Weathered planks cross a wide breathing marsh where tidewater rises through grass and old roof tiles. Terrecester’s chimneys show beyond a line of watchlamps.

room.name: Kobold Raft Reeds
room.description: Dozens of tiny reed rafts are lashed between cattails. Painted dragon masks grin from the prows, and powder horns hang just above the tide line.

room.name: Reefmist Shrine
room.description: A low shrine of driftwood and mother-of-pearl honors sailors who never returned. Its lamp has gone dark, though fresh footprints show someone still visits.

object.name: Dark Reef Lamp
object.description: The shrine lamp has no oil, and the tide marks around it look like finger bones.
object.missing_item_text: The lamp needs a sealed oil cruse before it can be relit.
object.interact_text: You refill and light the lamp. The fog offshore withdraws from the breakwater for a few precious hours.
object.completed_text: The reef lamp already burns with a steady blue flame.

room.name: Terrecester Wharf: South Gate
room.description: Salt-stained walls, hanging nets, and patched ballistae frame the southern gate of Terrecester Wharf. League guards count every cart twice because pirates have learned to hide inside honest cargo.

room.name: Cedar Net Yard
room.description: Halibut nets, sailcloth, and crab pots hang between cedar poles. Families mend holes while watching the sea with the wary patience of people used to alarms.

room.name: Tidebound Barracks
room.description: The barracks smells of oiled leather, wet wool, and crossbow strings. A map of pirate approach lanes covers one wall under a dozen angry knife marks.

room.name: Signal Platform
room.description: From the tower platform, colored shutters can warn the whole harbor. Several shutters have been loosened, giving false all-clear signs to ships below.

room.name: Barracks Armory
room.description: Racks of boarding pikes, oilskins, and harpoon bolts line the walls. The lockbox for emergency fuses is empty.

room.name: Terrecester Wharf: Harbor Market
room.description: Terrecester’s market sprawls across plank streets over black water. Fishmongers, rope sellers, League auditors, refugees, sailors, smugglers, and sea-priests all shout under the same gulls.

room.name: Terrecester Ferry Ticket Office
room.description: A blue-painted ticket office overlooks the tide pier. Its brass clerk-window is open, its ledger dry, and its sign very clear: Hearthwatch sales are suspended; Terrecester sells the coastal passage.

object.name: Tidebound Ferry Policy Board
object.description: The board lists fare rules, tide delays, and penalties for boarding without a stamped ticket.
object.interact_text: You confirm the fast ferry is intentionally locked behind Terrecester purchase to prevent eastbound travelers from bypassing the coast road.
object.completed_text: The ferry policy has already been copied into your journal.

room.name: Terrecester Tidepier
room.description: The pier stretches into gray-green water toward a waiting Tidebound ferry. Bells mark outgoing tides while deckhands load mailbags for Hearthwatch and wounded sailors coming home from the Glendes patrol.

room.name: Ferry Watchtower
room.description: A narrow tower watches both the harbor and the ferry lane inland. The Hearthwatch ticket office is visible only as a distant shuttered square in the mind of anyone who has made the crossing.

room.name: Tidebound Ferry: Hearthwatch Crossing Run
room.description: The ferry cuts through mist, river-mouth current, and open coastal chop in a single strange route known only to Tidebound pilots. The passage exists for returning travelers, not for skipping the Marches.

object.name: Stamped Ticket Check
object.description: A deckhand taps the blue stamp on each traveler’s ticket before the ferry leaves the pier.
object.missing_item_text: The crew refuses boarding without a Terrecester-issued ferry ticket.
object.interact_text: Your Terrecester-issued ticket is accepted, and the ferry bell rings for passage.
object.completed_text: The ferry crew already recognizes your stamped ticket.

room.name: Fishmarket Arcade
room.description: Stalls of eel, cod, shellfish, kelp wine, and illegal pearls fill a covered arcade. League auditors pretend not to smell the smuggling under the legitimate fish.

room.name: Customs House of Salt and Scale
room.description: Ledgers, confiscated blades, and sealed sea-chests crowd the customs house. A privateer warrant with the wrong signature has everyone nervous.

room.name: Kelpcook Kitchens
room.description: Steam pours from iron pots of fish stew, kelp noodles, and spiced crab. Refugee children carry bowls to sailors who are too tired to sit upright.

room.name: Shipwright Lane
room.description: Sawhorses, tar pots, keel timbers, and half-finished skiffs fill a narrow lane. The shipwrights work under guard because pirates have started cutting ropes at midnight.

room.name: The Long Ropewalk
room.description: Hemp ropes stretch the length of the lane under swinging lanterns. One strand has been cut and reknotted with a pirate’s sailor-knot.

room.name: League Drydock
room.description: A cracked patrol cutter rests in the drydock, its hull scored by kobold grapnels and human ballista bolts. The workers have chalked insults directly onto the damage.

room.name: Captain’s Green
room.description: A wind-bent green at the top of the wharf holds command tents, memorial stones, and a tide-clock. Tidebound captains argue here beneath a statue of a woman holding a lantern and a knife.

room.name: Tidebound League Hall
room.description: The hall is equal parts courthouse, counting house, and war room. Every chair is bolted down, a tradition from the year captains settled policy by throwing furniture.

room.name: League Chart Room
room.description: Sea charts cover the walls in overlapping layers of ink, pins, and red string. The Glendes Islands are marked with a spiral and the words: old ruin, older oath.

room.name: Wharf Magehouse
room.description: The magehouse studies tide-glass, ship wards, and the irritating habit of coastal ghosts to correct navigation charts after midnight.

room.name: Temple of the Returning Tide
room.description: An open-air temple faces the Thesmeda Sea. Priests bless vessels, mourn the drowned, and ask the tide to return only what belongs to the living.

room.name: Storm Cellar Beneath the Temple
room.description: The storm cellar stores candles, shrouds, salt, and old relic-rubbings recovered from the Glendes Islands by sailors who refused to go back.

room.name: Outer Breakwater Under Bombardment
room.description: Wave-smashed stones curve around the harbor mouth. Kobold rafts dart between swells while human privateers fire from captured cutters beyond the shoals.

room.name: Privateer Bombardment Line
room.description: Smoke hangs low over the water where enemy boats trade signals with shore spies. The smell of powder and salt makes every breath taste metallic.

room.name: Skiff Launch to the Glendes Islands
room.description: A narrow launch ramp points toward the island chain. Tidebound pilots will not leave without a Glendes chart and a good reason to risk the crossing.

object.name: Glendes Crossing Chart
object.description: A waterproof chart shows reef teeth, pirate drift lanes, and the narrow safe passage to the buried ruin.
object.missing_item_text: The pilot wants a proper Glendes chart before crossing.
object.interact_text: You mark the crossing route and convince the pilot the voyage can be made.
object.completed_text: The Glendes route is already marked.

room.name: Thesmeda Sea Crossing
room.description: The skiff rises and falls through slate water between Terrecester and the Glendes Islands. Dark shapes move beneath the hull, too broad to be fish.

room.name: Glendes Islands: East Beach
room.description: A crescent beach of black sand and broken shells curves below old ruin-stones. Pirate fires gutter behind wreckage dragged above the tide.

room.name: Shellbone Cove
room.description: The cove is carpeted with white shells and whale bones carved into warnings. Some warnings are new; some are old enough to predate Terrecester itself.

room.name: Wrecked Privateer Camp
room.description: A human-kobold privateer camp lies smashed as if something massive passed through without hurrying. The survivors fled inland, leaving maps and blood in equal measure.

room.name: Glendes Island Jungle Path
room.description: Salt-twisted trees grip old flagstones. Birds go silent whenever the ruin’s buried stones hum beneath the roots.

room.name: Overgrown Terrace Trap Cache
room.description: An overgrown terrace hides spring-blades and a dry cache sealed in wax. The trap is old, patient, and still very rude.

room.name: Tide-Pool Grotto
room.description: A grotto of clear tide pools reflects a ceiling of roots and ruin-stone. Something has scratched a maze diagram into the wet wall with a claw.

room.name: Buried Labyrinth: Ruin Forecourt
room.description: Half the ruin is swallowed by sand and salt grass. A serpent-shaped lintel coils above the entrance, its stone eyes turned toward the sea rather than the intruder.

room.name: The Buried Labyrinth: Sunken Entry
room.description: The entry passage descends under the island into cool stone. Sand runs down the walls in thin lines, and each footstep echoes from the wrong direction.

room.name: Labyrinth Dead End: Sand Chute
room.description: A sloped chute ends in a bowl of dry sand under a cracked ceiling. Coins, bones, and broken compass needles show how often explorers mistook this for progress.

room.name: Buried Labyrinth: Compass Hall
room.description: A circular hall bears eight worn compass roses, though only four directions still mean anything. Channels in the floor pull loose sand toward unseen machinery.

object.name: Salt-Worn Compass Rose
object.description: The compass rose shows a serpent crossing itself three times before reaching a pearl.
object.interact_text: You memorize the warning: the direct path is bait, and the worthiest route folds back on itself.
object.completed_text: The compass warning has already been studied.

room.name: Buried Labyrinth: Mirrored Trench
room.description: A waist-high trench of black water mirrors a ceiling that is not there. Some reflections move a heartbeat late.

room.name: Trap Drop: Pitch-Black Cistern
room.description: A false floor drops into an old cistern. The ladder is intact, but the water holds armor scraps, pale crabs, and a smell like opened graves.

room.name: Underwater Sluice Cache
room.description: A submerged side chamber hides waxed bundles wedged between stone sluices. The cache rewards anyone stubborn enough to climb out of the trap the long way.

room.name: Buried Labyrinth: Tidal Gallery
room.description: Sea water breathes in and out through carved vents. Each tide changes which floor stones are slick, safe, or secretly hinged.

room.name: Gallery Supply Cache
room.description: A small chamber holds emergency supplies left by a doomed Tidebound survey crew. Their notes stop after the phrase “the serpent is still choosing.”

room.name: Crab Crypt
room.description: Ancient graves have been invaded by pale crabs wearing rings like crowns. The dead seem less angry than embarrassed.

room.name: Buried Labyrinth: Serpent Tile Walk
room.description: Green-black tiles form a serpent whose body crosses the corridor in impossible knots. Stepping on the wrong scale snaps darts from the walls.

room.name: Scissor-Gate Crossing
room.description: Two bronze gate-blades slide open and shut with the rhythm of waves. The walls are scarred where armor, packs, and one unfortunate hat were cut in half.

room.name: False Sanctuary of Dry Stone
room.description: A beautiful dry chamber pretends to be the shrine. Its altar is too clean, its candles too new, and its painted serpent has human eyes.

room.name: Drowned Reliquary Dead End
room.description: This reliquary dead-ends in brackish water and shattered bronze icons. The trap is not that it kills intruders; the trap is that treasure makes them stay.

room.name: Lower Crossing of Three Floods
room.description: Three corridors meet over ankle-deep water. Tide marks on the walls show different heights from the same hour, as if the labyrinth cannot agree with itself.

room.name: Submerged Underpath
room.description: A crawlspace runs beneath the crossing through cold water and barnacle-choked stone. It bypasses the most obvious doors but not the things living below them.

room.name: Hidden Pearl Cache
room.description: A narrow pocket opens behind the underpath where ancient divers hid pearls, oilskin maps, and a sea-glass focus before the ruin sank into legend.

room.name: The Knot Crossing
room.description: The passage folds into a stone knot. North sounds like south, east smells like the sea, and the floor has too many old bloodstains to be purely decorative.

room.name: Rope Bridge Over the Buried Chasm
room.description: A rope bridge crosses a vertical shaft full of salt fog. Every plank is numbered, and several numbers are missing.

room.name: Obsidian Drop Dead End
room.description: The bridge ends at a glossy black drop with no visible bottom. A dead explorer’s chalk mark reads: “not this way, unless falling is your plan.”

room.name: The Buried Labyrinth: Saltblind Maze
room.description: A chamber of low walls, salt haze, and repeating serpent murals shifts whenever the tide sighs. The true path is remembered by rhythm rather than sight.

maze.progress_message: The salt haze thins as you follow the tide-serpent’s folded path.
maze.failure_message: A wrong turn fills the chamber with white glare and returns you to the first serpent mural.
maze.success_message: The haze collapses inward, revealing a narrow threshold marked with a pearl-shaped socket.

room.name: Threshold of the Worthy Tide
room.description: Beyond the saltblind maze stands a calm threshold where the dungeon finally stops trying to kill the impatient. The air tastes of old judgment and clean rain.

room.name: Antechamber of the Tide-Eyed
room.description: A long room curves like a ribcage before the final sanctum. Pearl scales are set into the walls, each engraved with a name of someone the sea returned.

room.name: Sanctum of Eshdru, the Tide-Eyed
room.description: A flooded sanctum opens beneath a broken dome where moonlight falls through seawater. Eshdru coils around the Tidecrown Pearl, ancient, scarred, and less enemy than final question.

object.name: Tidecrown Pearl Pedestal
object.description: The Tidecrown Pearl rests in a cradle of old coral and serpent bone. It does not glow for greed, only for earned passage.
object.interact_text: You claim the Tidecrown Pearl after Eshdru accepts your worthiness, and the sea around the sanctum briefly goes still.
object.completed_text: The Tidecrown Pearl has already been claimed from its coral cradle.

room.name: Glendes North Landing
room.description: A hidden landing lies beyond the serpent sanctum, opening to a cliff trail no pirate fleet has ever found. From here the road climbs toward the storm country.

room.name: Duskfall North Cliff Road
room.description: The coastal trail climbs above the Thesmeda Sea until salt wind becomes cold mountain air. Behind you lies Terrecester and the Glendes maze; ahead, the road rises toward Thundervale Peaks.

room.name: Stormbreak Foothills
room.description: The coastal cliff road gives way to black pine, blue scree, and air charged enough to raise hair from skin. Above the foothills, Thundervale Peaks rise in stepped walls where lightning walks the ridges before thunder is heard.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

object.name: Stormbreak Waystone
object.description: A giant-sized milestone has been cut down and repurposed by shepherds. Runes show a stormlift, a thunderforge, and an aegis-shaped sign.
object.interact_text: You trace the runes and learn the old ascent: foothills, switchback, bridge, giant road, lower hold, stormlift, thunderforge.
object.completed_text: The waystone still names the ascent in giant runes and shepherd chalk.

room.name: Windsplit Shepherd Path
room.description: A narrow side path winds through bell-hung fenceposts. The bells are practical, not decorative: if lightning strikes the wrong ridge, the ringing tells herders which way to run.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Sky-Goat Pastures
room.description: Hardy goats crop thundergrass beside slate shelters roofed with copper mesh. Children have tied blue ribbons to the horns of the oldest animals so no one mistakes them for ordinary livestock.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

object.name: Lost Bell Line
object.description: A snapped bell line lies under trampled grass, its copper hooks bent by something with hands.
object.interact_text: You gather the bell hooks and prove the attack was staged to scatter the herds toward the switchback.
object.completed_text: The repaired bell line rings clearly when the wind shifts.

room.name: Stormgoat Shelter
room.description: The shelter smells of wool, wet slate, and medicinal smoke. A wall map marks safe caves, lightning funnels, and ridge graves no sensible climber visits during cloud-dark.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: East Rune Outcrop
room.description: A half-buried giant rune juts from the pasture ridge. Its grooves collect rainwater even under a clear sky, as if the stone remembers storms not yet born.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Pilgrim’s Switchback: Lower Turn
room.description: Prayer flags snap along a steep ascending road. Each flag names a traveler who survived the pass and left a warning for the next pair of boots.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Old Switchback Cache
room.description: A shallow cave behind a waterfall of wind holds emergency stores. Someone recently pried open the good crates and left only broken splints and Cabal wax.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Pilgrim’s Switchback: Upper Turn
room.description: The road narrows until two wagons could not pass without politeness or a funeral. Far above, giant-built arches appear and vanish inside moving stormcloud.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Shepherd’s Eyrie Gate
room.description: A gate of pine, copper nails, and braided yak-hair rope guards the mortal settlement clinging to the mountainside. The guards bow to the storm before they acknowledge visitors.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Shepherd’s Eyrie Common
room.description: Houses lean into the cliff on stilts and stone braces. Rope bridges connect kitchens, shrines, workshops, and sleeping lofts above a communal fire kept under a copper rain hood.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

object.name: Storm-Season Notice Board
object.description: Weather watches, lost bells, bridge warnings, and giant-sighting marks crowd the board.
object.interact_text: You learn the Eyrie fears three things at once: unnatural storms, raiders on the bridge, and the giants mistaking mortal panic for mortal guilt.
object.completed_text: The notice board still rattles with new storm warnings.

room.name: Stormwatch Inn
room.description: The inn is built around a stone chimney struck by lightning so often it has become a local calendar. Climbers, herders, Marchwardens, and quiet giant-servants drink thick tea under thunderproof shutters.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Eyrie Rope-Market
room.description: Copper hooks, stormglass lenses, salted cheese, leather masks, barometer shells, and prayer-kites hang from rope stalls above a drop no merchant seems concerned about.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Skyhook Ropewalk
room.description: Rope-makers braid yak hair, linen, and conductive wire into storm-safe climbing lines. The walkway sways so gently that the movement becomes more unnerving than a proper shake.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Shrine of the First Thunder
room.description: A shrine has been carved into a ledge barely wide enough for kneeling. Offerings are weighted with stones so the wind cannot steal prayers before the thunder hears them.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Griffon Perch
room.description: An old perch platform hangs over the valley. Griffons wheel far above, respected but not owned; the Eyrie keeps treaties with them, not stables.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: High-Wind Roost
room.description: The roost is a broad shelf of white stone scoured clean by wind. Feathers the size of shields lie wedged between rocks beside old giant handprints.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Thunderfall Bridge: South Anchorage
room.description: The bridge begins at a tower of old giant masonry. Rain falls upward along one side of the stones, proof that the mountain has stopped respecting ordinary rules.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Thunderfall Bridge: Open Span
room.description: A stone bridge wide enough for giants crosses a gorge where thunder pools like water. Lightning forks below the bridge, then climbs upward in pale veins.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

object.name: Bridge Grounding Chain
object.description: A broken chain of sky-iron links dangles from the span into the thunder gorge.
object.interact_text: You brace the chain with a sky-iron piton and calm the worst lightning crawling across the bridge stones.
object.completed_text: The repaired chain hums a steady warning instead of screaming with every bolt.

room.name: Thunderfall Underbridge
room.description: Maintenance arches run beneath the bridge, sized for giant apprentices and mortal fools. Wind drags sparks along the ceiling like fish in a river.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Rain-Rune Cleft
room.description: A narrow cleft holds a rain-rune wedged into black stone. Water beads on the rune in perfect lines, spelling a giant warning about storms that learn names.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Thunderfall Bridge: North Anchorage
room.description: The far anchorage is scarred by fresh blast marks. A Cabal campfire still smokes inside an old giant bootprint, a careless insult no storm giant would ignore.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Lightning-Scarred Raider Camp
room.description: Cabal canvas and stolen shepherd rope lie scorched in a hollow. The raiders were harvesting sky-iron from bridge scars and packing it with black wax seals.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Giant-Step Causeway
room.description: The causeway is made of individual stones larger than cottages. Mortal trails zigzag across each step, turning a giant’s straight road into a day’s climb.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Overlook of Vhal Torunn
room.description: From this wind-carved balcony, Vhal Torunn appears above the peaks: lower halls rooted in granite, upper towers suspended inside slow-turning stormcloud.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Broken Storm-Rune Terrace
room.description: A terrace of carved runes has been hammered open from below. The damage is precise, surgical, and cruel: someone wanted the mountain’s weather to bleed.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

object.name: Broken Storm-Rune
object.description: The rune once dispersed lightning across the peaks. Cabal marks now twist it into a summoning wound.
object.interact_text: You copy the corruption pattern and learn that the storm is being driven from the Hollow Thunderforge.
object.completed_text: The broken rune continues to drip rain that smells faintly of ash.

room.name: Lower Vhal Torunn Gate
room.description: Twin doors of blue granite stand beneath a lintel carved with a storm giant hand withholding lightning. The scale of the gate makes every mortal argument sound temporary.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Lower Vhal Torunn Hall
room.description: The lower hall is not abandoned; it is reserved. Giant benches, rain basins, and copper braziers sit ready for visitors who know how to be small without being cowardly.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Cloud-Smith Workbench
room.description: A workshop table the size of a bridge bears rune chisels, lens chains, stormglass, and a half-repaired stormlift sigil. Mortal tools have been laid nearby as an act of consideration.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Prophecy Steps
room.description: Steps climb through a shaft open to the sky. Rain falls in slow spirals here, pausing near carved prophecies as though trying to read them.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Lower Tempest Archive
room.description: Stone shelves hold storm records, not books: frozen lightning, jars of first rain, thunder knots, and slabs naming weather events older than human kingdoms.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.

room.name: Rune Index Gallery
room.description: A gallery of rotating rune-stones indexes the mountain’s defenses. One empty socket is labeled in Giant: ASCENT SIGIL—RETURN BEFORE NEXT DEAD STAR.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Audience Beneath Thunder
room.description: Three storm giant seats face a mortal speaking-circle no larger than a dining table. The arrangement is intimidating but fair; the circle is exactly where echoes carry best.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Oracle Balcony
room.description: The balcony looks out beneath the cloud layer. Each thunderclap reveals, for a blink, the outline of paths that do not exist until the storm permits them.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Stormlift Base
room.description: A circular platform of stormglass and sky-iron waits in a shaft that vanishes into cloud. The lift is silent until the right sigil wakes its runes.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

object.name: Stormlift Console
object.description: A giant console holds a sigil socket surrounded by weather-runes for lift, balance, mercy, and judgment.
object.interact_text: You set the Charged Stormlift Sigil into place. The shaft fills with blue light, and the platform begins breathing upward with the storm.
object.completed_text: The stormlift hums with a steady ascent pattern.
object.missing_item_text: The console remains inert. Orvanth said the sigil must be charged with recovered storm-rune components before the lift will rise.

room.name: Upper Stormlift Landing
room.description: The Stormlift breaks through the cloud ceiling into cold gold light. The platform rests against battlements that hang between mountain and storm as if both agreed to share the same stone.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Upper Rain Court
room.description: Rain falls in separate curtains around the court, each one a different temperature and color. Storm giant attendants read the curtains like ledgers.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Cloud-Hung Battlements
room.description: Battlements float from the mountain wall on stormglass anchors. Below them, the world is hidden by a sea of cloud; above them, the Hollow Thunderforge pulses with corpse-blue light.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Cloud Cache Lintel
room.description: A hollow behind the battlement lintel holds offerings left by giant apprentices: practical tools, weather charms, and one apology carved into sky-iron.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.
The giants are not absent. They are watching from above the thunderline.

room.name: Tempest Archive
room.description: The upper archive is a cathedral of weather records. Every shelf hums with a storm that already happened, and every table is chained in case prophecy gets windy.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.

room.name: Sky-Throne Anteroom
room.description: A quiet anteroom waits before the closed sky-throne. The giants do not open it during crisis; rulership, here, is slower than lightning and heavier than thunder.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.

room.name: Hollow Thunderforge Gate

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.

object.name: Giant Warning Slab
object.description: The slab warns that the forge regulates weather, not weapons. Later hands have scratched Cabal diagrams over the warning.
object.interact_text: You confirm the Cabal is abusing a weather-engine to bind storm spirits and animate the dead.
object.completed_text: The warning slab remains scarred by Cabal corrections.

room.name: The Hollow Thunderforge: Entry Vault
room.description: The dungeon begins inside a giant-sized lock chamber where rain evaporates before touching the floor. Old maintenance grooves lead deeper into the mountain’s storm engine.

room.name: The Hollow Thunderforge: Giant Hall

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.

room.name: The Hollow Thunderforge: False Ore Spur
room.description: This dead-end spur once stored conductor ore. Now it holds only scraped wall marks, broken picks, and a cache tucked behind a cracked rune.

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.

room.name: The Hollow Thunderforge: Maintenance Tunnels

companion_dialogue.line: This is not a road so much as a storm deciding whether travelers deserve a path.

room.name: The Hollow Thunderforge: Tool Cache
room.description: A tool cache has been missed by the Cabal because the latch is labeled in shepherd marks rather than Giant. Someone small was once expected to maintain this place too.
